l4_steps.name: Identify expiring crew certifications
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records, certificate expiry calendar
l4_steps.output: List of crew members with certifications expiring within 90 days
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of expiring certs identified ≥60 days before expiry
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen qualification module requires manual reconciliation with FAA IACRA records; mismatches cause last-minute groundings when discrepancies surface during pre-flight checks

l4_steps.name: Map requirements against FAR/AQP framework
l4_steps.input: Expiry list, FAR Part 61/63/65 requirements, airline AQP approval document
l4_steps.output: Per-crew training requirement matrix (type rating, recurrent, PC, OE, SEP)
l4_steps.kpi: Requirement matrix accuracy ≥99% vs. FAA-approved AQP schedule
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with FAA-approved AQP have different recurrency intervals than standard FAR Part 135/121 defaults; Jeppesen must be manually configured per AQP module or will generate false compliance gaps

l4_steps.name: Validate requirements against fleet qualification matrix
l4_steps.input: Training requirement matrix, aircraft type endorsements per crew member
l4_steps.output: Validated training plan with fleet-specific simulator variant assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Zero invalid simulator variant assignments at time of booking
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet commonality assumptions (e.g. 737-700 vs. 737 MAX 8 differences) can result in incorrect simulator type bookings; reconfigured MAX simulators require separate certification after Boeing grounding

l4_steps.name: Generate training schedule and crew assignments
l4_steps.input: Validated training plan, simulator availability calendar, crew contract bid periods
l4_steps.output: Draft training schedule with crew-to-session assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Training schedule published ≥45 days before earliest session date
l4_steps.pain_point: CAE SimFinity scheduling does not natively integrate with Jeppesen rostering; double-bookings arise when crew are simultaneously assigned to flying duties and simulator sessions during the same duty period

l4_steps.name: Check crew scheduling conflicts and FAR legality
l4_steps.input: Draft training schedule, current crew pairing and rostering data
l4_steps.output: Conflict-free training assignments with FAR Part 117 rest compliance confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Zero training assignments that violate FAR Part 117 rest or duty limits
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator sessions count as duty time under FAR Part 117 but are often omitted from crew duty calculators; non-compliance discovered late in scheduling cycle forces expensive last-minute crew swaps

l4_steps.name: Reserve simulator slots and instructor resources
l4_steps.input: Conflict-free training assignments, simulator capacity at CAE/FlightSafety facilities
l4_steps.output: Confirmed simulator reservations and instructor assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Simulator utilisation rate ≥85%; booking cancellation rate ≤5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Industry-wide simulator capacity constraints (limited Level D 737 MAX simulators globally) cause lead times of 6–12 weeks; last-minute certificate expirations cannot be accommodated without costly wet-lease of third-party simulator time

l4_steps.name: Notify crew of training assignments and prerequisites
l4_steps.input: Confirmed simulator reservations, eLearning pre-requisite course list
l4_steps.output: Training notification delivered to crew via crew portal; pre-study materials assigned in LMS
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acknowledgement of training assignment ≥95% within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew portal notification fatigue leads to missed acknowledgements; no escalation workflow in SAP SuccessFactors Learning to flag non-response to crew base managers automatically

l4_steps.name: Deliver CBT and ground school modules
l4_steps.input: Crew training assignment, eLearning modules (systems, procedures, emergency)
l4_steps.output: Completed CBT records with pass/fail scores per module
l4_steps.kpi: CBT completion rate ≥98% before simulator session; average CBT pass rate ≥90% on first attempt
l4_steps.pain_point: CBT content refresh lags behind Boeing and Airbus service bulletin cycles; crews may train on outdated emergency procedure content if LMS version control is not tightly managed with OEM curriculum releases

l4_steps.name: Execute simulator training session (PC/OE/LOFT)
l4_steps.input: Simulator briefing pack, AQP Maneuvers Requirements Table (MRT), crew pairing for session
l4_steps.output: Completed simulator session log with performance ratings per MRT maneuver
l4_steps.kpi: Session completion rate ≥97%; average maneuver proficiency score ≥3.0/4.0 on CAST/AQP rubric
l4_steps.pain_point: CAE SimFinity session logs are stored locally at training centre; real-time sync to Jeppesen qualification records requires manual file export and upload, creating a 24–48h data latency window during which crew show as non-current in scheduling systems

l4_steps.name: Verify attendance and training hours compliance
l4_steps.input: Simulator session logs, ground school attendance records
l4_steps.output: Verified training completion certificate with total contact hours
l4_steps.kpi: Attendance verification completed within 24h of session end; zero incomplete records forwarded to assessment phase
l4_steps.pain_point: Partial session completions (e.g. simulator hardware fault mid-session) require FAA Operations Specification deviation approval before credit can be granted; no automated workflow in SAP SuccessFactors to flag partial completions for regulatory review

l4_steps.name: Administer written and oral knowledge exam
l4_steps.input: Completed ground school record, FAA-approved question bank
l4_steps.output: Exam result with pass/fail determination and topic-level breakdown
l4_steps.kpi: Exam pass rate ≥92% on first attempt; remedial re-exam scheduled within 7 days of failure
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA-approved question banks must be updated within 30 days of regulatory change (e.g. new NOTAM format, amended AOM chapter); SAP SuccessFactors Learning has no automated content update trigger linked to ATPCO or FAA rulemaking RSS feeds

l4_steps.name: Evaluate simulator checkride performance
l4_steps.input: AQP Maneuvers Requirements Table, simulator session video/data replay
l4_steps.output: Proficiency Check (PC) evaluation form; pass/fail recommendation per AQP standards
l4_steps.kpi: Checkride pass rate ≥95% on first attempt; debrief delivered within 1h of session end
l4_steps.pain_point: Under AQP, unsatisfactory grades must be correlated across crew cohorts to identify systemic training gaps vs. individual performance issues; CAE SimFinity does not natively produce cohort-level analytics — requires separate export to AWS Redshift for trend analysis

l4_steps.name: Process pass/fail outcome and assign remedial path
l4_steps.input: PC evaluation form, exam results, crew training history
l4_steps.output: Pass: qualification advancement triggered. Fail: remedial training plan with timeline and restricted flying status applied
l4_steps.kpi: Remedial plan issued within 24h of failure; restricted flying status applied in Jeppesen within 2h of fail determination
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen does not automatically restrict crew from scheduled flights upon a failed checkride — manual status update required; delay in status change creates legal exposure if a non-current crew member departs before the block is applied

l4_steps.name: Issue or renew certificate and update qualification record
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application)
l4_steps.input: Passed PC evaluation form, current pilot certificate data, airline training records
l4_steps.output: Updated FAA airman record; renewed type rating or recurrent certification on file
l4_steps.kpi: Certificate updated in FAA IACRA within 5 business days of checkride pass; zero expired certificates active in Jeppesen qualification module
l4_steps.pain_point: IACRA processing delays (common during peak season or after mass recurrent training cycles) can leave pilots in a limbo state — passed checkride but no updated certificate — requiring Temporary Authorisation letters that must be manually tracked outside automated systems

l4_steps.name: Sync updated qualifications to crew scheduling system
l4_steps.input: Updated FAA IACRA record, CAE SimFinity training completion data
l4_steps.output: Crew qualification profile updated in Jeppesen; crew cleared for line flying on qualified fleet type
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification sync completed within 4h of IACRA update; scheduling legality check auto-passed in Jeppesen within same window
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen qualification record sync relies on manual CSV import from FAA IACRA; no API integration exists, creating a reconciliation bottleneck during high-volume recurrent training months (typically January and July for most carriers)

l4_steps.name: Monitor upcoming recurrency expiry dates
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification profiles, recurrency interval rules (FAR 121.433, AQP cycle)
l4_steps.output: Rolling 90-day expiry dashboard updated daily; crew at-risk list generated
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of expiring qualifications flagged ≥60 days before expiry; dashboard refresh latency ≤1h
l4_steps.pain_point: AQP recurrency windows are qualification-event-based (not calendar-based), making rolling expiry calculation complex; Jeppesen's standard recurrency alert module applies calendar logic and generates false alarms for AQP-credentialed crew, reducing alert credibility

l4_steps.name: Trigger automated recurrency alert to crew and base manager
l4_steps.input: At-risk crew list, crew contact directory, base manager hierarchy
l4_steps.output: Automated alert sent to crew member (60-day) and base manager (30-day); training scheduling re-triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Alert delivery confirmation rate ≥99%; training re-scheduling initiated within 3 business days of 60-day alert
l4_steps.pain_point: Alert fatigue from Jeppesen's notification volume causes base managers to filter or ignore automated messages; no read-receipt or escalation logic exists in standard Jeppesen notification module — critical alerts are indistinguishable from routine operational messages

l4_steps.name: Escalate non-compliant crew to Crew Compliance team
l4_steps.input: Unresolved expiry alerts, crew scheduling status, FAA compliance reporting requirements
l4_steps.output: Non-compliant crew grounded in Jeppesen; compliance incident logged; corrective action plan issued to Director of Operations
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew operating with lapsed certifications; escalation-to-grounding action completed within 2h of SLA breach
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Certificate Management Office requires airlines to self-report systemic training programme non-compliance within 10 days; failure to ground and report non-compliant crew can trigger enforcement action under 14 CFR Part 13, including civil penalties up to $25,000 per violation per day
